headline: Wall Street posts modest back-to-back losses as long-term sovereign bond yields soar to multi-decade peaks, completely offsetting a sharp decline in international crude oil and dovish commentary from Federal Reserve officials. U.S. stock benchmarks drifted lower on Tuesday as the fixed-income market continued to exert a tight grip on equity valuations. Investors faced an intensifying duration squeeze as the 30-year U.S. bond yield rocketed to 5.594%—its highest point since 2002—while the benchmark 10-year Treasury yield climbed to 5.293%, matching levels not seen since June 2007. The spike in long-term yields overshadowed a welcoming 2.6% slide in Brent crude futures to $102.59 a barrel alongside a drop in August JOLTS job openings to 7.079 million. Equities managed to pare their steepest intraday losses after New York Fed President John Williams cooled aggressive near-term rate hike expectations, prompting a pullback in the short-duration 2-year yield.
